entries.effect: the class resolves: an application that links strongly against UIEventAttribution names _OBJC_CLASS_$_UIEventAttribution and dyld finds it. What a caller on this release gets is the whole of what the class is for - build one from the four values it was given, read them back, copy it - and NOT a link preview: the only producer of an attribution is the system opening one, and there is no path to that here (no SafariServices, no link-preview extension, neither of which exists on 6.1.3 or 4.3). The rows say so rather than claiming a preview flow this release has no path to
entries.source: the SDK that declares these names, toolchain/.agent-work/sdk-26.2's iPhoneOS26.2.sdk System/Library/Frameworks/UIKit.framework/Headers/UIEventAttribution.h and UIEventAttributionView.h, which are byte for byte the Mac Catalyst ones after comments and availability macros are stripped - and are also in the 16.4 SDK this package compiles against, so nothing is redeclared here, exactly as UIButtonConfiguration.m redeclares nothing for UIButtonConfiguration; the answers are the host's own under Mac Catalyst 27.0 build 26A428, read by the probe in .agent-work/runs/b2/ and held to the port by the case in tests/backports/host/uikit2/eventattribution_test.m (32 checks, 0 failures); the port's object is packages/frameworks/apple-backports/UIKit/UIEventAttribution145.m, compiled for armv7-apple-ios6.1.3 and armv7-apple-ios4.3 with 0 lines matching " error: "

entries.effect: the class resolves, and what an instance is on this release is an inert non-interactive rectangle: opaque YES, user interaction NO, no background colour, no subviews, not an accessibility element - all four measured on the host and all four written, including the two that differ from UIView's own defaults. There is nothing for it to draw, because the only thing that ever put an attribution on screen was a link preview and there is none here
